claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is governed by interactions among grain boundaries, lattice distortion, and short-range order.
Grain boundaries, lattice distortion, and short-range order control dislocation activity during deformation.
Grain boundaries, lattice distortion, and short-range order control phase transformations during deformation.
The initial high-entropy-alloy multilayer contains FCC and BCC phases.
The material retains a nanoscale multilayer coating.
Sustained loading will increase dislocation density relative to the initial state.
Sustained loading will induce a phase transformation relative to the initial state.
Sustained loading will increase lattice distortion relative to the initial state.
The increases in dislocation density and lattice distortion, together with phase transformation, lead to progressive plastic deformation.
The effects of compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order on deformation behavior are not fully understood.
In-situ transmission electron microscopy can be used to observe microstructural evolution during deformation.
Failure to observe significant increases in dislocation density, phase transformation, and lattice distortion during sustained loading would falsify the hypothesis.
